recommendations.target_segment: Month-to-month subscribers in early tenure (1-12 months)
recommendations.descriptive_evidence: Month-to-month accounts span 3,875 customers (55.02% of base) at 42.71% churn (95% CI [41.16%, 44.27%]), accounting for 88.55% of all churn and $120,847.10/mo in historical monthly billing of churned records. The narrowed 1-12 mo subset (n=1,994, 28.31% of base) churns at 51.35% (1,024 churners = 54.79% of all churn).
recommendations.diagnostic_evidence: Contract has the strongest categorical association with Churn (chi2=1184.6, Cramer's V=0.4101, Holm p=9.97e-257), followed by tenure_tier (V=0.3512). Controlling for covariates, Two-year contracts show adjusted OR=0.2602 vs Month-to-month.
recommendations.predictive_evidence: Raw-column test permutation ranks Contract #1 (dROC-AUC=0.0428) and tenure #2 (dROC-AUC=0.0256). Test Tier 1 (p>=0.50, n=275) realizes 67.27% churn.
recommendations.proposed_action: Launch structured first-90-day onboarding check-ins and test step-down annual contract migration incentives (e.g., locked rate or waived upgrade fee) specifically among Model Tier 1 & Tier 2 early-tenure accounts.
recommendations.assumptions_and_caveats: Assumes contract-migration incentives achieve an assumed 15-25% relative churn reduction without eroding net margin; IBM data is cross-sectional and does not test experimental discount elasticity.

recommendations.target_segment: Fiber optic subscribers lacking OnlineSecurity or TechSupport
recommendations.descriptive_evidence: Within broad Fiber optic accounts (n=3,096, 41.89% churn, $114,300.05/mo historical churned billing), the narrowed target cohort lacking OnlineSecurity or TechSupport comprises n=2,722 accounts (38.65% of base) with 45.70% churn (95% CI [43.84%, 47.58%], 1,244 churners = 66.56% of all churn, $108,733.60/mo historical churned billing). Those lacking both add-ons (n=1,765) churn at 55.01% vs 14.17% for Fiber users with both (n=374).
recommendations.diagnostic_evidence: OnlineSecurity (V=0.3474), TechSupport (V=0.3429), and InternetService (V=0.3225) rank 3rd-5th in association strength. Even after controlling for tenure and contract, Fiber optic retains adjusted OR=2.5646, whereas OnlineSecurity_Yes (OR=0.6913) and TechSupport_Yes (OR=0.7099) remain protective.
recommendations.predictive_evidence: InternetService ranks #3 (dROC-AUC=0.0162), OnlineSecurity ranks #5, and TechSupport ranks #6 in held-out Random Forest permutation importance.
recommendations.proposed_action: Audit Fiber optic service reliability/price perception and pilot bundled OnlineSecurity + priority TechSupport packages at no extra promotional cost for 3-6 months on Tier 1/2 Fiber accounts lacking both add-ons.
recommendations.assumptions_and_caveats: Assumes lack of add-ons reflects unaddressed perceived value rather than pure unmeasured customer stickiness bias (existing add-on holders may reflect self-selected loyal subscribers rather than causal add-on protection).

recommendations.descriptive_evidence: Electronic check accounts (n=2,365, 33.58% of base) churn at 45.29% (95% CI [43.29%, 47.30%], $84,288.75/mo historical churned billing) vs 15.24% for Credit card automatic payers — accounting for 57.30% of all churn.
recommendations.diagnostic_evidence: PaymentMethod shows strong bivariate dependence (chi2=648.1, V=0.3034, Holm p=4.42e-139). After controlling for contract, tenure, and charges, Electronic check retains an elevated adjusted OR=1.3601.
recommendations.predictive_evidence: PaymentMethod ranks #7 (dROC-AUC=0.0022) in held-out test importance and helps separate Tier 2 Elevated Risk accounts (41.96% actual churn) from Tier 3 Low Risk.
recommendations.proposed_action: Promote streamlined enrollment into automatic credit card or bank transfer autopay with small one-time billing credits paired with clear paperless payment reminders.
recommendations.assumptions_and_caveats: Assumes payment-method switching reduces accidental/bill-shock churn rather than merely selecting already loyal customers.

recommendations.target_segment: Hold-out accounts exceeding CV F1-optimal cutoff (p >= 0.33)
recommendations.descriptive_evidence: Baseline full-sample churn is 26.54% (n=1,869 / 7,043) with $139,130.85/mo historical billing across churned records (30.50% of total monthly billing); untargeted outreach wastes 73.46% of contacts on non-churners.
recommendations.diagnostic_evidence: Multivariate churn risk spans Contract (V=0.4101), tenure_tier (V=0.3512), OnlineSecurity (V=0.3474), and PaymentMethod (V=0.3034); a calibrated probability threshold integrates all risk factors simultaneously without arbitrary single-variable exclusions.
recommendations.predictive_evidence: Random Forest (Test ROC-AUC=0.8440, PR-AUC=0.6513, Brier=0.1361) at CV F1-optimal cutoff tau=0.33 flags n=499/1,409 (35.42%) test accounts (Tier 1 p>=0.50: n=275, 67.27% realized churn; Tier 2 0.33<=p<0.50: n=224, 41.96% churn), capturing 74.60% of test churners (279/374) at 55.91% precision (F1=0.6392) vs Tier 3 Low Risk (10.44% churn).
recommendations.proposed_action: Use probability-threshold triage when outreach budget scales to ~35% of base: route Tier 1 (p>=0.50) to high-touch agent outreach, Tier 2 (0.33<=p<0.50) to automated digital offers, and exclude Tier 3 (p<0.33).
recommendations.assumptions_and_caveats: Distinct from a fixed Top-30% budget queue (see REC-5). Model trained on fictional cross-sectional snapshot; live deployment requires A/B uplift validation and periodic calibration monitoring.

recommendations.target_segment: Top 30% capacity-ranked risk queue (empirical test cutoff p >= 0.3918)
recommendations.descriptive_evidence: In the full snapshot, churned records carry $139,130.85/mo in historical monthly charges ($64.76 avg across all vs $74.44 among churned), making volume-capped prioritization critical when retention team capacity is strictly budgeted below the 35.42% F1-threshold share.
recommendations.diagnostic_evidence: High-risk concentration within short-tenure Fiber and Month-to-month segments creates steep diminishing marginal risk in the bottom 70% of accounts, supporting ranked queue ordering by calibrated churn probability.
recommendations.predictive_evidence: Ranking the sealed 1,409 test accounts by Random Forest probability selects n=423 (30.02% capacity, min predicted p=0.3918), capturing 246/374 (65.78%) test churners at 58.16% precision (2.19x lift over random) and covering $18,907.85/mo (69.48% of the $27,214.90/mo historical churned billing in test).
recommendations.proposed_action: When outreach team capacity is fixed at <=30% of accounts (~2,113 seats if scaled proportionally across a 7,043-customer base as an illustrative benchmark), rank customers descending by predicted probability and contact the top-30% queue rather than using the looser 0.33 cutoff.
recommendations.assumptions_and_caveats: Observed lift (2.19x) is measured strictly on n=423/1,409 held-out test records; illustrative 6-mo net financial scenarios ($15-$25 cost, 10%-30% save rate) depend on untested causal uplift assumptions.

chart_inventory.title: Observed Churn Rates Across Contract Type and Payment Method (N = 7,043)
chart_inventory.axis_labels: X: Contract / PaymentMethod; Y: Churn Rate (%) with 95% Wilson CI
chart_inventory.legend_applicable: Yes (Sample average reference line; color vs sample mean)
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Month-to-month subscribers exhibit a 42.71% churn rate (n=3,875), compared with 2.83% on Two-year contracts (n=1,695).
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Customers paying via Electronic check show a 45.29% churn rate (n=2,365), more than triple the 15.24%–16.71% rates of automatic bank transfer and credit card groups.

chart_inventory.title: Empirical Distributions and KDE Curves of Numeric Predictors Stratified by Churn
chart_inventory.axis_labels: X: Customer Tenure (Months) / Monthly Charges (USD) / Total Charges (USD); Y: Probability Density
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Churned subscribers cluster heavily at short tenure (median 10.0 months vs. 38.0 months for retained customers; rank-biserial r = -0.4797).
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Churned customers pay noticeably higher MonthlyCharges (median $79.65 vs. $64.43; p < 0.0001), whereas lower TotalCharges among churners reflects shorter duration.

chart_inventory.title: Price Dispersion Across Contract Types Stratified by Churn Outcome
chart_inventory.axis_labels: X: Contract Type; Y: Monthly Charges (USD) / Total Charges (USD)
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Within the high-risk Month-to-month tier, churners pay a higher median monthly bill ($79.05) than retained peers ($64.95).
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: TotalCharges increases sharply across Contract tiers primarily because multi-year contracts correspond to substantially longer accumulated tenure rather than lower monthly bills.

chart_inventory.title: Violin Density Comparison of Tenure Across Contract and Internet Regimes
chart_inventory.axis_labels: X: Contract Type / Internet Service Type; Y: Customer Tenure (Months)
chart_inventory.legend_applicable: Yes (Split halves: Churn = No vs Yes)
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Split violin shapes reveal that Month-to-month and Fiber-optic churn concentrates in a sharp early-tenure spike (1–12 months), whereas retained One-year and Two-year customers cluster near 60–72 months.
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Even on long-term contracts, the rare churners sit at much higher tenure than Month-to-month churners, confirming strong interaction between contract lock-in and survival duration.

chart_inventory.title: Joint Tenure vs. Monthly Charges Density Stratified by Churn Outcome
chart_inventory.axis_labels: X: Customer Tenure (Months); Y: Monthly Charges (USD); Colorbar: Customer Count
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Churned density peaks sharply in the upper-left high-price/early-tenure quadrant (tenure <= 12 mo and MonthlyCharges >= $70), where observed churn reaches 68.07% (n=880).
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Retained customers bifurcate into a low-cost baseline band (~$20/month across all tenures, mainly no-internet phone users) and a high-tenure, high-spend loyalty cluster above 48 months.

chart_inventory.variables: Cramer's V across predictors; Contract x tenure_tier -> Churn
chart_inventory.title: Diagnostic Association Strength and Stratified Contract-Tenure Churn Heatmap
chart_inventory.axis_labels: Left: Predictor vs Cramer's V; Right X: Tenure Tier, Y: Contract Type
chart_inventory.legend_applicable: Yes (Colorbars for Cramer's V and Churn Rate %)
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Contract (Contract: V=0.410), tenure_tier (V=0.351), and protective add-ons (OnlineSecurity, TechSupport) exhibit the strongest bivariate associations with Churn.
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Across all segments, Month-to-month subscribers in months 1-12 combine large volume and extreme risk (51.4% churn across n=1,994 accounts).

chart_inventory.variables: Predicted churn probabilities vs actual Churn (Test set n=1,409)
chart_inventory.title: Held-Out Test Discrimination and Calibration Benchmarks (n = 1,409)
chart_inventory.axis_labels: ROC: FPR vs TPR; PR: Recall vs Precision; Calibration: Mean Pred Prob vs Observed Fraction
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: On the untouched hold-out test set (n=1,409), Logistic Regression achieves ROC-AUC=0.8412 (PR-AUC=0.6286) compared with 0.8440 (PR-AUC=0.6513) for Random Forest.
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Calibration curves track near the diagonal (champion Brier=0.1361, ECE=0.0173), indicating well-calibrated probabilities for tier ranking.

chart_inventory.variables: Actual Churn vs Predicted Churn across thresholds
chart_inventory.title: Held-Out Test Confusion Matrices Across Cutoff Regimes (n = 1,409; Churn = 374)
chart_inventory.axis_labels: X: Predicted Class; Y: Actual Class
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: At default 0.50 cutoff, Random Forest catches 185 of 374 test churners (Recall=0.495, FN=189, Precision=0.673).
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Lowering the cutoff to the validation-tuned threshold tau=0.33 raises test Recall to 0.746 (279/374 churners detected, F1=0.639) at the expense of 220 false positives.

chart_inventory.variables: 19 raw predictors vs held-out ROC-AUC drop & logistic log-odds
chart_inventory.title: Predictive Model Explainability: Global Feature Importance and Directional Effects
chart_inventory.axis_labels: Left X: Mean ROC-AUC Decrease; Right X: Log-Odds Coefficient
chart_inventory.legend_applicable: No (Color encodes positive vs negative churn risk direction)
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Permuting raw features on the hold-out test set confirms Contract (dROC-AUC=0.0428), tenure (0.0256), and InternetService (0.0162) dominate Random Forest discrimination.
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: Regularized logistic regression aligns with diagnostics: Month-to-month contracts, Fiber optic internet, and short tenure sharply elevate log-odds of churn, while multi-year contracts and OnlineSecurity/TechSupport reduce risk.

chart_inventory.variables: Top-K% risk outreach vs captured churn recall; capacity x save rate -> illustrative net value
chart_inventory.title: Prescriptive Prioritization: Cumulative Test Capture Gain and Labeled Scenario Sensitivity
chart_inventory.axis_labels: Left: % Population Targeted vs % Churners Reached; Right: Assumed Save Rate vs Outreach Capacity
chart_inventory.legend_applicable: Yes (Model ranking vs Random baseline; Net Value colorbar)
chart_inventory.interpretation_1: Ranking held-out customers by calibrated Random Forest scores enables reaching 65.78% of all churning accounts (246/374) within the top 30% capacity tier (2.19x lift over random).
chart_inventory.interpretation_2: The right panel demonstrates that illustrative 6-month retention value remains strictly contingent on assumed save rates (10%-30%) and outreach costs ($15/customer), underscoring the need for randomized retention testing.
